title: The Empty Chair
moral: Compassion means remembering people when they are not with us and making them feel that they still matter.

pages.text:
Every Thursday, Class Four had story circle.

The children sat on the carpet, and one child read aloud from the big blue storybook. Everyone liked story circle because Mrs. D'Souza also allowed quiet snacks.

"Quiet snacks means no crunchy chips," she always said.

Still, Rohan once brought papad pieces.

Every bite sounded like a tiny chair breaking.

This Thursday, there was one empty chair near the window.

It belonged to Amina.

Amina had been absent for three days. She was usually the first to raise her hand, the first to laugh, and the first to say, "I know what happens next!" even when she did not.

"Maybe she is still sick," said Tara.

Story circle began, but Nikhil kept looking at the empty chair. The room felt different without Amina's small laugh.

At lunch, Mrs. D'Souza placed a box on the table.

"Amina is recovering at home," she said. "Would anyone like to make a get-well card?"

Many children nodded, but after lunch, football started outside. One by one, children ran to the ground.

Nikhil loved football too. His team needed him.

He picked up his shoes.

Then he looked at the empty chair again.

Amina had once shared her crayons with him when his red pencil broke. She had drawn a terrible dinosaur on his notebook to make him laugh. It looked like a lizard wearing a crown.

Nikhil sat down.

He drew a big card. On the front, he wrote:

Story circle is not the same without you.

Inside, he drew every child sitting on the carpet. He even drew Amina's empty chair near the window.

Then he added the crowned lizard.

Soon, Tara came back from the ground.

"What is that?" she asked.

"A dinosaur," said Nikhil.

Tara looked closely. "It needs medical help."

They both laughed.

By the end of the day, the whole class had signed the card.

The next Monday, Amina came back.

Her face was still a little pale, but when she saw the card, her eyes became bright.

She touched the drawing of the empty chair.

"You saved my place," she whispered.

Nikhil smiled. "Of course."

During story circle, Amina sat in her chair again.

This time, when she laughed, the whole room felt full.
